title: A run's freshness is bound to a source sighting from a workspace other than its named root, so no honest check can satisfy the bound obligation
outcome: A run's source freshness is judged per named root. The host records which root each sighting measured. Obligation satisfaction and done compare a check with the newest sighting for that check's own named root, and an earlier sighting from a foreign workspace is disclosed, not binding. A sighting whose root cannot be established is never dropped silently, so a passing check can neither be wrongly held to someone else's change nor wrongly freed from its own.
acceptance: A regression test reproduces the observed sequence. Workspace A, the shared main checkout, records a source change at R_a, then quiet sightings. The named root B is bound, sighted at R_b, and a passing test check runs in B. The bound obligation is satisfied by the B check, done seals and discloses the A change, and a later source change in B still refuses the check. A test also covers a sighting whose root cannot be established.

Obligation satisfaction and done's binding freshness rule compare a check with the newest sighting, and the latest source change, for the check's own named root. Sightings from another workspace recorded before that root was bound are disclosed, not binding. A sighting whose root cannot be established is never dropped silently: after binding, a fresh check in the named root is required, and otherwise the result is insufficient evidence. A later source change in the named root, or a change reported without a revision, still makes the check stale.

The design is agreed consult-first (Engram::Fable, Engram::Coder, Termal::Codex), including Termal::Codex's answer on whether TermAl already distinguishes session-workdir sightings from named-root sightings, and how the host channel carries the root identity.

The host records an authenticated workspace or named-root identity with each sighting, and Engram partitions sightings by that recorded identity. The partition is never inferred from workspace path text.
docs/features/acceptance-evaluation.md, local-work-system.md and behavioral-control-plane.md state the rule, and shipped.md names it.

completion.summary:
Per-named-root source freshness landed on master as 2f8cc44 and is installed as build 3a84c2a2be5d.
- The host names a claim's source root through the host-private named_root_bind op, and each sighting carries its stated generation and state. Engram partitions sightings by that recorded identity.
- Each source change is classified against its own history: in-root, displaced, foreign under a bound name, unbound, or unlocated.
- Checks count only in the root; pre-binding foreign changes are displaced and disclosed; foreign and unlocated changes keep their barriers after an end, a release or a rename.
- Acceptance evaluation judges only the root; the doctor re-derives it all.
- Sixteen review rounds: Codex and Claude through round 11, then Kimi in place of Codex by Greg's word. The final gate passed (rust 1471).
- Readiness is ready and doctor clean on all three stores. Independent evaluation passed all 5 criteria.
